transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. My laboratory analysis on the spent coolant drums, completed yesterday, found 2.4% chlorinated solvent content. Per our site's waste matrix, any batch at or above 1.0% chlorinated solvent must be routed to hazardous-liquid treatment rather than ordinary coolant recycling. This result has not yet been attached to the waste authorization documentation.

transcript.text: I need to share something relevant to the shipment controls. I confirmed with the disposal contractor that their tanker permit limits us to no more than 8 of these drums per load. So the 14 drums will need to go out as two separate shipments: a first load of 8 and a second load of 6. I received this permit condition in the contractor's service email but haven't entered it into the transport booking system yet.

transcript.text: I need to disclose a critical finding from my warehouse inspection. I found active seepage at the base of exactly 4 of the 14 spent coolant drums. Those 4 drums must each be placed in a UN-rated overpack before any movement. The other 10 drums can remain on their existing spill pallets. I recorded this inspection on the shift clipboard, but I want to flag that the waste file has not yet been updated with this information.
